recipes.name: Monte Cristo inspired by American Dad
ingredients: For the Monte Cristo Pate en Croute
For the Monte Cristo Patty Melt
3 tbsp raspberry jam + more for serving
instructions: For the Classic Monte Cristo
Combine the egg, milk, and salt in a shallow bowl. Whisk to combine, then set aside. - 1 whole large egg - 2 tbsp whole milk - ¼ tsp kosher salt
Spread the mustard and mayonnaise on the side of one piece of bread, and the raspberry jam on the other. - 2 slices white bread - tbsp ~1 dijon mustard - tbsp ~1 mayonnaise - 2 ½ tbsp raspberry jam

Add one slice of swiss cheese to the mayo/mustard slice of bread, then layer the turkey and ham over top. - 2 slice(s) deli swiss cheese - tbsp ~1 dijon mustard - tbsp ~1 mayonnaise - 2 slices deli turkey - 2 slices deli ham
Add another slice of swiss over the ham, then place the other slice of bread (jam side down) over the cheese.
Dip each side of the sandwich into the egg mixture, letting it soak in for about 15-20 seconds on each side.

Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the egg-soaked sandwich to the skillet and cook on both sides until golden brown, crispy, and the cheese has melted, about 3-4 minutes. - 2 tbsp unsalted butter
Serve with a dusting of powdered sugar. - As needed powdered sugar
For the Monte Cristo Pate en Croute

Melt the butter in a medium skillet. Add the shallot and cook until translucent, about 2-3 minutes. Add the garlic and continue to cook for 30 seconds or until fragrant. - 1 tbsp unsalted butter - 1 small shallot minced - 3 garlic cloves minced
Add the wine to the pan and continue to cook until the wine has reduced by about 50%. Turn off the heat and set aside to cool. - 30 g dry white wine

Combine the pork shoulder, turkey breast, and smoked pancetta in a bowl. Add the salt, pink curing salt, sugar, peppers, thyme, sage, madeira, cognac, and cooled shallot mixture to the bowl. Fold the mixture to thoroughly combine the ingredients. - 350 g pork shoulder coarsely ground - 225 g turkey breast diced - 175 g smoked pancetta diced - 9 g kosher salt - 2 ¼ g pink curing salt - 4 g sugar - 1 g freshly ground black pepper - ½ g white pepper - 1 tbsp fresh thyme finely minced - 2 tsp fresh sage finely minced - 30 g madeira - 30 g cognac
Cover the surface of the meat mixture with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 24 hours.
The next day, preheat the oven to 375 °F with convection. Place a baking steel on the bottom rack of the oven while preheating.
Remove the meat mixture from the refrigerator and fold the egg into the meat mixture. - 1 whole large egg
Spray a 8 ½ inch by 4 ½ inch baking tin with a generous coating of nonstick cooking spray.
Line the greased baking tin with the rolled out Pastry Crust. Use any extra dough to help press out any folds in the dough. - Pastry Crust (see recipe below)
Fill the pastry cavity with the meat filling. Top with the pastry lid and seal shut the edges with a decorative crimp.
Brush the top of the pate en croute with Egg Wash. Optionally, using the back of a paring knife to score the top with a decorative pattern. - Egg Wash (see recipe below)
Using two large round pastry tips, cut out two equidistant rounds from the top of the pastry. Place the metal tips into the vacated holes to act as vents.

Bake the pate en croute for 15 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 325 °F. Continue baking for 45-60 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown and the internal temperature of the pate reaches 165 °F. If the filling is cooked but the top isn’t browned enough, increase the temperature to 400 °F with convection and continue to cook for 5 minutes or until the top is well browned.
Allow the pate en croute to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate until completely cold.

Pour the Raspberry Aspic into the vents using the pastry tips as funnels. Remove the pastry tips, then return the pate en croute to the refrigerator until the aspic is set, about 2-4 hours. - Raspberry Aspic (see recipe below)

Unmold the pate en croute, then slice and serve cold or at room temperature with Cheese Foam, whole grain mustard, and pickles. - Cheese Foam (see recipe below) - As needed dill pickle chips - As needed wholegrain mustard
For the Pastry Crust
Adapted from
Great British Chefs Hot Water Crust Pastry
Combine the flour and salt in a large bowl. Whisk to combine, then make a well in the center of the flour and set aside. - 1000 g all purpose flour - 1 tbsp kosher salt
Bring the lard and water to a simmer. - 250 g lard - 525 g water
Pour the heated lard mixture into the flour well and stir to combine. Then, knead the dough until smooth, about 5 minutes.
Cover and let the dough rest for 20 minutes before rolling out.
When ready to use, remove ⅓ of the dough and set aside in plastic wrap for the lid. Roll out the remaining ⅔ of the dough to a rectangle about 14 inches long, 10.5 inches wide, and ¼ inch thick.
Roll the lid out to a rectangle 9 inches long, 5 inches wide, and ¼ thick thick.
For the Egg Wash
Combine the egg, egg yolk, and salt in a small bowl. Whisk until the egg wash is homogenous. - 1 whole egg - 1 egg yolk - 1 pinch kosher salt
Refrigerate until ready to use.
For the Raspberry Aspic
Combine the water and raspberry jam in a small saucepot. Bring the mixture to a simmer. - 400 g water - 50 g good quality raspberry jam

Meanwhile, soak the gelatin sheets in cold water, completely submerged, for 6 minutes. Once bloomed, remove the sheets from the water and squeeze out the excess water. - 7 sheets gold gelatin sheets - As needed cold water
Once at a simmer, turn off the heat and stir in the bloomed gelatin sheets.
Pour the still warm raspberry aspic into the vents of the Pate en Croute.
Refrigerate the Pate en Croute until the aspic is set, about 2-4 hours.
For the Cheese Foam
Whisk to combinet he salt, pepper, and xathan gum in a small bowl. - 1 tsp kosher salt - ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper - ⅛ tsp xanthan gum
Heat the milk in a small saucepot until simmering. Turn off the heat, then stir in the swiss cheese. Allow the mixture to sit for 10 minutes. - 360 ml whole milk - 200 g swiss cheese grated

Transfer the cheese mixture, salt mixture, and heavy cream to a blender. Blend until the mixture is completely smooth, then pour it into an isi whip canister. Charge the barrel with 2 nitrous-oxide chargers, then screw on the lid tightly. - 120 ml heavy cream
Gently shake the canister. Refrigerate overnight before serving cold.
For the Monte Cristo Patty Melt
Form the ground turkey into an oval patty about the size of the rye bread slices and set aside. - 7 oz ground turkey
Preheat a large skillet with neutral oil over low heat. Add the sliced onion and cook for 30 minutes or until the onions are well caramelized. - 2 tbsp neutral oil - 1 vidalia onion thinly sliced
Transfer the caramelized onions to medium bowl and stir in the raspberry jam. Set aside until ready to use. - 3 tbsp raspberry jam + more for serving

Heat the remaining tablespoon of neutral oil in a large non-stick skillet. Add the turkey patty and cook for 3-5 minutes per side or until browned. Cover the mostly cooked burger with swiss cheese and grated guryere cheese. Add the water to the skillet, then cover immediately to steam the cheese and finish cooking the patty, about 2-3 minutes. Turn off the heat and set aside. - 1 tbsp neutral oil - 2 slices swiss cheese - ¼ cup gruyere cheese shredded
Spread mayonnaise and mustard on one the slice of bread, then spread the caramelized onion mixture onto the other slice. - 2 pieces hearty rye bread - 2 tsp mayonnaise - 1 ½ tsp dijon mustard
Add the ham onto of the mayo/mustard slice and top the onion slice with the turkey patty. Then, bring the two slices of bread together to form the sandwich. - 3 oz maple ham
In a large shallow dish, whisk together the egg, milk, and salt. - 1 whole egg - 2 tbsp whole milk - ¼ tsp kosher salt
Dredge the assembled sandwich in the egg mixture.
Melt the butter in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the dredged sandwich to the skillet and cook on each side for 3-4 minutes or until well browned. - 2 tbsp unsalted butter
Slice and serve immediately with a dusting of powdered sugar and an extra dollop of raspberry jam.
